questions.question: A company deploys a generative AI chatbot for customer service and later argues in an incident report that "it wasn't a bug, the AI just made a mistake, which is different." How should a tester challenge this framing?

options.A: It's still a defect to investigate, whatever term is used to describe it
options.B: Only outputs that crash the underlying server should ever be logged as defects
options.C: AI systems should be exempt from all defect tracking and root-cause analysis processes
options.D: The framing is correct, since AI-generated mistakes can never be counted as software defects

questions.explanation: Calling a wrong or harmful output a "mistake" rather than a "bug" does not change that it is undesired behavior worth investigating, tracking and, where possible, mitigating like any other defect.

questions.question: An insurer classifies its automated claims-approval AI as "high-risk" under a risk-tiered AI regulation. What is the most direct practical implication of this classification for testing?

options.A: More rigorous testing, documentation and evidence of adequate risk mitigation are likely required before deployment
options.B: The classification only affects marketing materials and has no bearing on testing activities
options.C: High-risk classification automatically halves the testing effort otherwise required
options.D: The system becomes exempt from any further testing, since regulators have already reviewed the risk tier

questions.explanation: Higher-risk classifications under frameworks like the EU AI Act typically come with heightened obligations around testing rigor, documentation and evidence, not a lighter compliance burden.

questions.question: A team building a self-learning recommendation engine that continues training on live user interactions after deployment must plan its test strategy differently from a team deploying a locked model. What is the key difference to plan for?

options.A: No further testing is needed after the initial release, since self-learning models improve automatically
options.B: The self-learning model requires no monitoring at all, unlike the always-monitored locked model
options.C: Both approaches require exactly identical testing strategies with no meaningful differences
options.D: Ongoing monitoring and retesting are needed since the model's behavior can keep changing after release

questions.explanation: Because a self-learning system's behavior evolves after deployment, one-time pre-release testing is insufficient; ongoing monitoring and periodic retesting are needed to catch behavior that drifts or degrades.

questions.question: A generative AI feature occasionally produces a different, contradictory answer to the exact same customer question asked minutes apart. A developer says "that's impossible, software is deterministic." What is the most accurate response?

options.A: The variation proves the system has no machine learning component and is purely rule-based
options.B: Non-determinism is illegal in all deployed generative AI systems and must be reported
options.C: Sampling and randomness make this valid, not proof of a bug
options.D: The developer is correct, and this behavior can only be explained by a serious hardware failure

questions.explanation: Sampling and other sources of randomness mean many generative systems can validly give different acceptable answers to the same prompt, which testers need to account for in how they design and interpret tests, rather than always treating variation as a functional bug.

questions.question: Two vendors describe their products as "AI-powered": one uses a large neural network trained on millions of examples, and the other uses a small set of hand-written if-then rules with no learning at all. What should a tester conclude about testing implications?

options.A: The rule-based system will always be harder to test than any neural network
options.B: Both systems require identical testing techniques, since both are marketed using the term AI
options.C: Very different testing approaches, since only one is truly a learned system
options.D: Marketing language always accurately reflects the underlying technical approach in every case

questions.explanation: Marketing terminology does not determine the actual underlying technology; a truly rule-based system is tested more like conventional software, while a genuinely learned model needs ML-specific techniques like input data and model testing.

questions.question: A safety-critical AI feature controlling part of an industrial process must allow an operator to disable it instantly if something looks wrong. Which quality characteristic is being addressed, and how would a tester verify it?

options.A: Maintainability; verify that the feature's source code is easy for developers to modify later
options.B: Portability; verify that the feature can be installed on a different brand of industrial hardware
options.C: Autonomy / human oversight; verify that a disable action reliably and quickly stops the AI-driven behavior
options.D: Co-existence; verify that the feature runs correctly alongside unrelated software applications

questions.explanation: The ability for a human to promptly override or halt an AI system's actions is exactly what autonomy and human-oversight characteristics address, and testing it means verifying the disable mechanism actually works reliably and fast.

questions.question: A stakeholder asks for "explainability" of a credit-scoring model. Which test approach most directly evaluates whether this requirement is met?

options.A: Check only that the model's training data was collected within the last twelve months
options.B: Reliably and quickly halting the AI-driven behavior on command
options.C: Check only that the model's overall accuracy exceeds a numeric threshold on a test set
options.D: Check only that the model's source code is written in a widely used programming language

questions.explanation: Explainability specifically concerns whether the reasoning behind a decision can be understood by relevant stakeholders, so testing it means checking that provided explanations are both accurate and genuinely comprehensible, not just checking unrelated attributes like accuracy or code language.

questions.question: Which pair of AI quality characteristics is most likely to be in tension for a highly accurate but "black box" deep learning model used for medical diagnosis?

options.A: Compatibility and usability, which are typically unrelated to model complexity
options.B: Portability and installability, which rarely conflict for any AI system
options.C: Time behavior and maintainability, which rarely conflict for any AI system
options.D: Functional suitability (accuracy) and transparency/explainability

questions.explanation: Highly complex models often achieve strong accuracy but are hard to explain, creating a genuine trade-off between functional suitability and transparency that testers and stakeholders must weigh, especially in high-stakes domains like medicine.

questions.question: Which robustness test would most directly assess an image classifier's resilience to real-world camera conditions, such as slight blur or overexposure?

options.A: Evaluating the total physical file size of the classifier's saved model weights
options.B: Evaluating how quickly the classifier's underlying source code compiles
options.C: Evaluating the classifier's accuracy only on the original, perfectly clean training images
options.D: Evaluating the classifier's accuracy on a test set with images deliberately blurred or overexposed

questions.explanation: Robustness testing specifically probes behavior under realistic degradations like blur or overexposure, which a test on only clean images or unrelated code and file-size checks would never reveal.

questions.question: An AI-based hiring tool must satisfy both "fairness" across demographic groups and "functional suitability" (accuracy at predicting job success). A team improves accuracy by adding a feature correlated with a protected attribute, worsening fairness. What does this illustrate?

options.A: Whether given explanations are accurate and genuinely understandable
options.B: Fairness is not a legitimate concern for any tool used in employment decisions
options.C: Fairness and accuracy always improve or worsen together and can never actually conflict
options.D: Accuracy should always be maximized regardless of any effect on fairness metrics

questions.explanation: This is a concrete example of quality characteristics in tension, where improving one measurably harmed the other, which is exactly the kind of trade-off that needs explicit stakeholder decision-making rather than being resolved by testing alone.

questions.question: A recruitment model shows 92% overall accuracy but selects far fewer qualified female candidates than male candidates from an equally qualified applicant pool. Which additional evaluation would have surfaced this issue earlier?

options.A: Switching the model's programming language from one framework to another
options.B: Increasing the number of training epochs used to build the original model
options.C: Recomputing the exact same overall accuracy figure using a larger volume of data
options.D: Accuracy/functional suitability and transparency/explainability

questions.explanation: Aggregate accuracy can mask a large disparity between subgroups; disaggregated evaluation by subgroup is specifically designed to catch exactly this kind of hidden fairness problem.

questions.question: For a spam filter with 5% spam prevalence, a model achieves precision of 95% and recall of 40%. What does this combination indicate about its behavior?

options.A: It flags almost every incoming message as spam, whether legitimate or not
options.B: It never makes any mistakes at all in classifying any message
options.C: Accuracy on images with realistic blur, glare or overexposure
options.D: It correctly identifies all of the actual spam messages that exist

questions.explanation: High precision with low recall means positive predictions are trustworthy, but the model is conservative and lets most real spam through undetected, which is an important behavior to communicate to stakeholders.

questions.question: Which use of a ROC curve and its AUC (area under the curve) is appropriate for evaluating a binary classifier?

options.A: A genuine trade-off stakeholders need to explicitly weigh
options.B: Measuring the total storage size of the model file saved to disk
options.C: Measuring how many features were originally used as input to the model
options.D: Measuring the exact physical training time taken to build the model

questions.explanation: A ROC curve and its AUC summarize a classifier's ability to distinguish between classes across every possible decision threshold, which is useful for comparing models independent of any single chosen threshold.

questions.question: A classifier's default decision threshold is 0.5, and the business wants fewer false negatives even if that means more false positives. What adjustment achieves this?

options.A: Lowering the classification threshold so more borderline cases are predicted as positive
options.B: Retraining the model from scratch using a completely different algorithm
options.C: Raising the classification threshold so fewer cases are predicted as positive overall
options.D: Increasing the physical amount of memory available to the serving infrastructure

questions.explanation: Lowering the threshold makes the model more willing to predict positive, which reduces missed positives (false negatives) at the cost of more false alarms (false positives), directly matching the stated business preference.

questions.question: A company's product catalog changes daily, and a support LLM must always cite current prices. Why would RAG be preferable to fine-tuning for this specific need?

options.A: Fine-tuning updates a model's knowledge automatically and instantly whenever the catalog changes
options.B: RAG retrieves current information at answer time, avoiding the need to retrain whenever prices change
options.C: Fine-tuning is always cheaper and faster to apply than adding a retrieval step
options.D: RAG permanently removes the pretrained model's ability to reason about any topic at all

questions.explanation: Because fine-tuning bakes information into weights that would need retraining for every price change, whereas RAG can pull fresh data at query time, RAG better fits fast-changing factual content.

questions.question: Why might a team choose a simpler logistic-regression model over a more complex gradient-boosted model for a regulated lending decision, even if the complex model is slightly more accurate?

options.A: The simpler model is easier to explain and justify to regulators and affected customers
options.B: Simpler models always require significantly more training data than complex ones
options.C: Complex models can never be deployed in any regulated industry under any law
options.D: Logistic regression models are always guaranteed to be more accurate in every scenario

questions.explanation: In regulated, high-stakes contexts, interpretability and the ability to justify individual decisions can outweigh a small accuracy gain from a harder-to-explain complex model.

questions.question: A model is trained with class weights because only 1 in 200 transactions is fraudulent. What is the purpose of using class weights here?

options.A: To reduce the total number of features the model considers when predicting
options.B: To make the model penalize mistakes on the rare fraud class more heavily during training
options.C: To make the model completely ignore the rare fraud class during training entirely
options.D: To physically balance the number of transactions processed per second by the server

questions.explanation: Class weighting increases the training penalty for errors on the minority class, encouraging the model to pay more attention to rare fraud cases than it otherwise would with unweighted training.

questions.question: A junior data scientist proposes tuning the learning-rate hyperparameter by repeatedly checking performance directly on the final test set until the best score is found. What is wrong with this plan?

options.A: The plan is fine as long as the learning rate is changed no more than three times total
options.B: Evaluating accuracy and selection rates separately by subgroup
options.C: Nothing is wrong, since the test set exists specifically for iterative hyperparameter tuning
options.D: The plan would work correctly only if the test set is larger than the training set

questions.explanation: Using the test set for iterative tuning decisions is exactly what the validation set exists to prevent; repeatedly optimizing against the test set makes its final score an overly optimistic, biased estimate.

questions.question: A generative model produces a confident, fluent, but entirely fabricated legal citation. What does this behavior best illustrate?

options.A: Hallucination, where a generative model produces plausible-sounding but incorrect or invented content
options.B: Overfitting, which specifically concerns a model's excessive fit to its own training data
options.C: Data drift, which specifically concerns a shift in input data after deployment
options.D: Underfitting, which specifically concerns a model failing to learn any pattern at all

questions.explanation: Hallucination describes confidently generated content that is fluent but factually wrong or invented, a distinct and well-known failure mode of generative language models that testers specifically probe for.

questions.question: Which evaluation approach is most appropriate for assessing a text-summarization feature's output quality, beyond simple exact-match string comparison?

options.A: Using metrics or human judgment that assess semantic similarity, coverage and coherence against reference summaries
options.B: Requiring the generated summary to be character-for-character identical to one single reference summary
options.C: Measuring only how quickly the summarization model returns its output
options.D: Counting only the exact total number of words in the generated summary

questions.explanation: Since many different summaries can validly capture the same source content, evaluation needs approaches that judge meaning, coverage and coherence rather than requiring an exact string match to one fixed reference.

questions.question: Which test would most directly assess the robustness of an image classifier used in a self-driving car's perception system?

options.A: Lowering the threshold, accepting more positives overall
options.B: Testing only the classifier's speed on a set of perfectly clean, unobstructed sample images
options.C: Testing only the color scheme of the dashboard that displays the classifier's output
options.D: Testing only whether the classifier's source code compiles without any syntax errors

questions.explanation: Robustness for a safety-critical perception system specifically concerns behavior under realistic adverse conditions, which perturbed test images directly probe, unlike code compilation or unrelated interface checks.

questions.question: A team must decide whether to use the model under test as its own oracle, checking its output for internal consistency, or use an independent reference. What is the main risk of the first approach?

options.A: It always requires significantly more computational resources than using an independent reference
options.B: It is impossible to implement for any kind of AI-based system whatsoever
options.C: When the domain needs a specific style or reasoning pattern, not just facts
options.D: It always produces results that are more accurate than any independent reference could give

questions.explanation: Checking a model's self-consistency can catch some issues, but a model that is systematically and consistently wrong would pass its own internal check, so an independent oracle or reference is needed to catch that kind of error.

questions.question: A tester designs "acceptable-range" checks for a house-price prediction model instead of requiring an exact predicted value. Why is this approach appropriate?

options.A: Exact-value checks are always trivially easy to define for any regression task
options.B: Acceptable-range checks are required by law for every regression model regardless of the domain
options.C: A simpler model is easier to explain and justify to regulators
options.D: Range checks always guarantee the model has no remaining defects of any kind

questions.explanation: Since a "correct" house price is inherently somewhat fuzzy and context-dependent, a range-based partial oracle gives a practical, checkable criterion without requiring one single precise expected number.

questions.question: Which is the strongest argument for independent (third-party) testing of a high-stakes AI system, such as one used in criminal sentencing recommendations?

options.A: Independent testers are legally required for every AI system regardless of its actual stakes
options.B: Independent testers bring a perspective less influenced by the assumptions of the original development team
options.C: Independent testing always costs significantly less than testing performed by the original developers
options.D: Independent testing removes the need for any testing performed by the development team itself

questions.explanation: A fresh perspective can catch assumptions and blind spots the original team may share, which matters especially for high-stakes, potentially biased decisions where independent scrutiny adds real value.

questions.question: A tester finds that timestamps in a newly received training batch are stored as text strings instead of the expected numeric format used elsewhere in the pipeline. Which test level does catching this issue belong to?

options.A: ML development testing, since format issues can only ever be found through code review
options.B: Model testing, since timestamp formatting only ever affects a model's accuracy metric
options.C: Input data testing, since it concerns the quality and format of data before it is used for training
options.D: System testing of an unrelated, conventionally coded part of the application

questions.explanation: Catching a data format inconsistency before it reaches training is squarely an input data testing concern, distinct from evaluating the trained model itself at the model test level.

questions.question: A self-driving perception system's ODD (operational design domain) excludes heavy snow, and testers spend most of their effort on snow scenarios anyway. What is the concern with this allocation of effort?

options.A: The ODD only matters for functional testing and has no bearing on test prioritization
options.B: Effort is being spent outside the system's defined operating conditions instead of on scenarios it is actually meant to handle
options.C: Snow scenarios should always receive the majority of testing effort regardless of the defined ODD
options.D: There is no concern, since testing conditions outside the ODD always provides the most valuable information

questions.explanation: Testing effort should be prioritized toward the conditions a system is actually designed and expected to handle; heavily testing an explicitly excluded scenario diverts effort from where confidence is actually needed.

questions.question: A team proposes "the model has trained for 100 epochs" as its sole release criterion for a new classifier. What is the strongest argument against this specific criterion?

options.A: Epoch count is the single most reliable predictor of a model's real-world performance
options.B: This criterion is ideal, since it removes any need to measure the model's actual output quality
options.C: Hallucination: fluent, confident, but invented content
options.D: One hundred epochs is always too few for any classifier to reach acceptable quality

questions.explanation: A criterion based purely on training duration says nothing about whether the resulting model actually meets performance, fairness or robustness expectations, which measurable, outcome-based criteria are needed to verify.

questions.question: A regression suite for an ML system should be re-run primarily under which of the following circumstances?

options.A: Only once, immediately after the very first version of the model is deployed
options.B: When the model, its training data, or a significant part of the pipeline changes
options.C: Only when a completely unrelated part of the company's website is updated
options.D: Never, since machine learning models cannot experience any behavioral regression

questions.explanation: Because model behavior depends on the model, its data and its pipeline, a meaningful change to any of these is exactly when a regression suite should be re-run to catch any newly introduced problems.

questions.question: Why is it important to include "negative" and "out-of-scope" prompts when testing a customer-service chatbot?

options.A: Negative prompts are only relevant to chatbots that have no natural language understanding at all
options.B: Out-of-scope prompts are guaranteed to never occur in any real production usage
options.C: To confirm the chatbot handles irrelevant, malicious or unsupported requests gracefully rather than failing badly
options.D: Testing with negative prompts always guarantees the chatbot will never produce a harmful response

questions.explanation: Real users inevitably send unexpected, off-topic or adversarial input, so testing how the chatbot handles these cases reveals whether it degrades gracefully rather than breaking or producing an unsafe response.

questions.question: Why might a tester intentionally use inputs from outside the training data's typical range when testing an ML model's robustness?

options.A: Because doing so always and automatically improves the model's underlying accuracy
options.B: It cannot catch a systematic error, since it never checks ground truth
options.C: Because out-of-distribution testing entirely replaces the need for in-distribution testing
options.D: Because such inputs are always guaranteed to be functionally impossible in a real deployed system

questions.explanation: Production systems inevitably encounter inputs unlike anything closely represented in training, so deliberately testing this scenario reveals whether the model degrades gracefully or produces unreliable output.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: A tester notices that a feature called "account_id" strongly predicts customer churn in a training dataset. What should this observation prompt?

options.A: Investigating for possible data leakage, since an account identifier should not causally relate to churn
options.B: Concluding that the model's accuracy will always be poor because of this single finding
options.C: Immediately accepting the feature as a genuinely useful, causally meaningful predictor
options.D: Removing all other features from the model, since one strong feature is always sufficient

questions.explanation: An identifier field having strong predictive power often signals that it inadvertently encodes information from after the prediction point, a form of data leakage, which needs to be investigated before trusting the model.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: A dataset for a global product contains 95% English text and 5% text in ten other languages combined. What is the most likely testing concern?

options.A: The dataset's language distribution has no bearing on the resulting model's actual behavior
options.B: The model will refuse to process the majority English text as a direct result of this imbalance
options.C: The model may perform noticeably worse for the underrepresented, non-English languages
options.D: The model will always perform identically well across every language regardless of its share of the data

questions.explanation: Severe underrepresentation of most languages relative to English creates a real risk that the model generalizes poorly for those languages, which is exactly the kind of representativeness gap input data testing should flag.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: Which is a sound way to test for label correctness at scale in a very large labeled dataset, when manually reviewing every label is impractical?

options.A: Assuming all labels are correct, since a large dataset is always accurately labeled
options.B: Auditing only the records where the model's own prediction happens to agree with the label
options.C: Auditing only the very first ten records that appear at the top of the dataset file
options.D: Auditing a statistically representative random sample of labels for accuracy

questions.explanation: A well-chosen random sample gives a statistically meaningful estimate of overall label quality without the impractical cost of checking every single record individually.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: A model reports 98% test accuracy during development, but production accuracy is only 71% once deployed. Data leakage between the training and test sets is suspected. Why would leakage produce exactly this pattern?

options.A: Leakage always makes test accuracy come out lower than the model's true production accuracy
options.B: A gap this large could only ever be explained by a hardware malfunction, never by leakage
options.C: Leakage has no relationship at all to any gap between test and production performance
options.D: Data quality checks on records before they're used for training

questions.explanation: When test information effectively leaks into training, the model can appear to perform far better on the test set than it actually generalizes, exactly the large, suspicious gap described here.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: A tester checks that a time-series model's train and test split is chronologically ordered, with test data strictly after training data in time. Why does this matter?

options.A: The requirement only applies to models predicting categorical, not numeric, outcomes
options.B: Chronological ordering has no bearing on the validity of any time-series model evaluation
options.C: Chronological splits always produce worse-looking test results than random splits
options.D: Confirm the system handles irrelevant or hostile input gracefully

questions.explanation: For time-dependent data, a random split can accidentally let the model "see" information from the future relative to some test points, so a strictly forward-in-time split is needed for a realistic evaluation.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: Synthetic data is proposed to fill gaps for a rare failure class with too few real examples. What should testers verify about this synthetic data before it is used?

options.A: That it is kept completely undocumented so its origin cannot be traced later
options.B: That it realistically reflects the characteristics of genuine examples of that rare class
options.C: That it is generated purely at random with no reference to the real rare class at all
options.D: That it makes up the majority of the entire dataset, outnumbering all real examples

questions.explanation: Synthetic data is only useful if it genuinely resembles the real phenomenon it stands in for; unrealistic synthetic examples could teach the model incorrect patterns rather than helpfully filling a real gap.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: Which check best addresses the risk of "data poisoning" in a pipeline that ingests data from an external, less-trusted source?

options.A: Trusting all incoming external data completely, since external sources are always reliable
options.B: Increasing the total volume of external data ingested without applying any additional checks
options.C: Validating and sanitizing incoming data against expected patterns before it is used for training
options.D: Removing all internal, trusted data sources so only external data remains in the pipeline

questions.explanation: Data poisoning involves an attacker deliberately injecting harmful data to corrupt a model's training, so validating and sanitizing data from less-trusted sources is a direct, relevant mitigation.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: A tester finds duplicate records that appear in both the training set and the test set of a dataset. What is the appropriate response?

options.A: Leave the duplicates in place, since duplicate records never have any effect on evaluation
options.B: Delete the entire dataset and refuse to proceed with any further testing
options.C: Add even more duplicate copies of the same records to both sets equally
options.D: Remove the duplicates from one of the two sets so the split remains genuinely independent

questions.explanation: Duplicates crossing the train and test boundary undermine the independence of the test set, similar to other data leakage, so removing them from one side restores a fair, unbiased evaluation.

questions.question: A monitoring dashboard shows model accuracy has fallen from 0.90 to 0.78 over three months in production, with no code changes deployed. What is the most likely cause to investigate first?

options.A: Underrepresentation relative to how it's actually used in production
options.B: An improvement in the model's underlying algorithm that occurred automatically
options.C: A reduction in the number of employees working on the data science team
options.D: A change to the model's source code that has not actually been deployed

questions.explanation: With no code changes but declining accuracy over time, a shift in the incoming data's characteristics relative to training data, drift, is the most likely and directly testable explanation to pursue first.

questions.question: A tester wants to detect overfitting during model testing without access to a completely separate, held-out test set. Which approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Evaluate the model only on the exact same data it was trained on and trust that single result
options.B: Skip evaluation entirely, since overfitting can never be detected without a completely new dataset
options.C: Assume the model cannot possibly be overfitting if its training accuracy is reasonably high
options.D: Use cross-validation to estimate how well the model generalizes across multiple different data splits

questions.explanation: Cross-validation reuses the available data across multiple splits to approximate how the model would perform on unseen data, providing a workable overfitting signal even without a dedicated test set.

questions.question: A tester designs a check for a sentiment model: adding a clearly neutral, unrelated sentence, such as a weather remark, to an already positive review should not flip the predicted sentiment to negative. What technique is this?

options.A: Metamorphic testing, using a relation between an input and a modified version of it
options.B: Calibration testing, since it always checks numeric confidence against real accuracy
options.C: Back-to-back testing, since it always compares two independently built systems
options.D: A/B testing, since it compares two different live model versions on real traffic

questions.explanation: Defining an expected relationship between an original input and a modified variant, without needing one exact expected sentiment label, is the defining feature of a metamorphic relation.

questions.question: During adversarial testing of a text classifier, replacing words with synonyms causes the predicted class to flip entirely, even though the meaning is essentially unchanged. What does this reveal?

options.A: An unrelated issue with the testing tool that has no bearing on the model itself
options.B: A desirable property, since sensitivity to any wording change always indicates a well-tuned model
options.C: Proof that the model has achieved perfect accuracy on its original training data
options.D: A robustness weakness, where small, meaning-preserving changes disproportionately affect the model's prediction

questions.explanation: If a near meaning-preserving substitution flips the prediction, the model is relying on brittle surface patterns rather than robust understanding, which adversarial testing is specifically designed to expose.

questions.question: An A/B test for a new recommendation model shows a clear lift in click-through rate, but nobody had agreed beforehand on what metric would decide the outcome. The team declares victory based on this one number. What is the risk in this sequence of events?

options.A: Declaring success after the fact is always exactly as rigorous as defining criteria beforehand
options.B: Chronological order avoids leaking future information backward
options.C: The risk only exists if the new model happens to be more expensive to run than the old one
options.D: There is no risk at all, since any statistically significant lift in any metric always justifies a rollout

questions.explanation: Deciding success criteria after seeing results invites choosing whichever metric looks good, while missing guardrail metrics, like a drop in longer-term satisfaction, that were never defined or checked.

questions.question: A model performs well overall but noticeably poorly on inputs from one specific hospital in a multi-site healthcare deployment. What testing approach would have caught this before deployment?

options.A: Evaluating model performance using only a single combined score across all hospitals
options.B: Assuming that all sites in a multi-site deployment will always behave identically
options.C: Skipping evaluation on any site that submitted a comparatively smaller volume of data
options.D: Evaluating model performance broken down by data source or site, not only in aggregate

questions.explanation: Aggregate performance can conceal a real, site-specific weakness, so segmenting evaluation by data source is exactly the kind of check that would have surfaced this uneven performance earlier.

questions.question: A medical triage model flags cases as "90% likely urgent," but among all cases it rates at that confidence, only 60% actually turn out to be urgent. What quality problem does this reveal?

options.A: Data drift, which only concerns changes in the input data distribution over time
options.B: Poor accuracy in an absolute sense, which is always identical in meaning to poor calibration
options.C: Validating and sanitizing untrusted incoming data before training
options.D: A labeling error, which only concerns incorrect ground-truth labels in training data

questions.explanation: This is a calibration problem: the stated confidence overstates the real likelihood of being correct at that confidence level, which is a distinct concern from overall accuracy and matters when downstream decisions rely on the confidence value itself.

questions.question: A drift monitor for a production model should ideally alert on which of the following?

options.A: Any single individual prediction that differs even slightly from the previous one made
options.B: A statistically meaningful shift in input feature distributions or output prediction patterns
options.C: The exact time of day at which the model happens to receive the most requests
options.D: The number of unrelated support tickets opened by customers in a given week

questions.explanation: Effective drift monitoring focuses on meaningful statistical shifts in the data or outputs over time, rather than trivial single-prediction variation or metrics unrelated to the model's actual input and output behavior.

questions.question: A loan-approval model hits its overall 90% accuracy target, but robustness testing shows small, unrelated formatting changes to the same application can flip approval decisions. Should the model be released, and why?

options.A: No; meeting the accuracy target does not offset a serious robustness weakness that undermines trust in the decisions
options.B: No; the model should be rejected purely because it uses a numeric accuracy target at all
options.C: Yes; any model that meets its stated accuracy target should always be released without further consideration
options.D: Yes; robustness only matters for models used in domains other than lending

questions.explanation: Accuracy is one dimension among several; a serious robustness flaw, like decisions flipping on irrelevant formatting changes, is a legitimate reason to withhold release even when the accuracy bar is met.

questions.question: A team reports "the model passed all its tests" but the tests only ran the same 20 hand-picked examples every single time. What is the main limitation of this claim?

options.A: A tiny, fixed, hand-picked sample cannot give confidence about performance on the true range of real inputs
options.B: Hand-picked examples are always guaranteed to be more representative than randomly sampled ones
options.C: Twenty examples are always more than sufficient to fully validate any machine learning model
options.D: Repeating the same examples every time always produces a more statistically valid conclusion

questions.explanation: A small, unchanging, hand-picked set risks being unrepresentative and can hide problems that only appear on the broader diversity of real inputs, so passing it provides only weak assurance.

questions.question: Which is the best description of "regression" in the context of testing a machine-learning model after a change?

options.A: A previously acceptable behavior or performance level that worsens after a model or pipeline change
options.B: The mathematical technique used internally to fit a linear regression model's coefficients
options.C: A permanent, irreversible decline in a model's performance that can never be fixed
options.D: Any machine-learning task that predicts a continuous numeric value as its output

questions.explanation: In this testing context, regression means a previously acceptable behavior getting worse after a change, echoing the conventional software meaning, and is distinct from the unrelated statistical technique of the same name.

questions.question: A confusion matrix on the test set shows many false positives for one particular class but very few for the others. What should this pattern prompt a tester to investigate?

options.A: Whether the model should immediately be retrained using a completely unrelated dataset
options.B: Whether the confusion matrix itself was calculated using an incorrect mathematical formula
options.C: Drift, since the world has diverged from training-time conditions
options.D: Whether the false positives are simply due to random chance and require no further investigation

questions.explanation: A class-specific error pattern like this points to something particular about that class, such as data scarcity or similarity to another class, which targeted investigation of the data and errors can usually explain.

questions.question: Which is an appropriate guardrail metric to monitor when A/B testing a new fraud-detection model against the current one?

options.A: The number of lines of code changed to implement the new model
options.B: Sharing the actual feature logic between training and serving
options.C: The physical file size of the new model compared with the current one
options.D: The number of unrelated customer support staff currently employed by the company

questions.explanation: A guardrail metric protects against an unacceptable side effect that the primary metric might miss; here, wrongly blocking legitimate transactions is exactly the kind of harm a fraud model's A/B test needs to watch for.

questions.question: A model shows high variance: retraining with a different random seed changes its predictions on many of the same test inputs. What does this instability suggest for testing strategy?

options.A: Instability of this kind is desirable and should always be maximized during development
options.B: A single training run's results should always be treated as fully definitive and final
options.C: Random seed variation always indicates a fundamental defect in the machine learning framework used
options.D: Multiple training runs or an ensemble view may be needed to understand and report the model's true, typical behavior

questions.explanation: When results vary meaningfully across seeds, evaluating and reporting from just one run can be misleading, so testing strategy should account for this variability, for example by considering multiple runs.

questions.question: Validation loss rises while training loss continues to fall over successive training epochs. What is happening, and what testing implication follows?

options.A: The model is underfitting, and training should continue for many more additional epochs
options.B: The two loss values are completely unrelated and this divergence pattern has no meaning
options.C: The training process has a bug that always makes both losses rise together in this pattern
options.D: Assess severity and scope, then decide on a proportionate fix

questions.explanation: A widening gap where training loss keeps improving but validation loss worsens is the classic overfitting signature, and it argues for using validation performance, not training loss alone, to judge and stop training.

questions.question: During ML development testing, verifying the reproducibility of a training run addresses which risk?

options.A: That the trained model will always achieve a higher accuracy than any previous version
options.B: That the model will never need to be retrained again once reproducibility is confirmed
options.C: Gradual drift, as real-world patterns diverge from training data
options.D: That the training data will automatically become perfectly representative of production

questions.explanation: Confirming reproducibility helps distinguish a genuine effect of a code or data change from mere run-to-run noise, which is essential for trusting comparisons between experiments.

questions.question: Which is the best example of a continuous-integration check specifically suited to an ML project, beyond typical software CI checks?

options.A: A check that verifies the company's logo displays correctly on the login page
options.B: A check that a data schema validation step correctly rejects a deliberately malformed sample input
options.C: A check that counts the total number of commits made to the repository
options.D: A check that measures how many people are currently subscribed to a project mailing list

questions.explanation: Validating that the pipeline actually rejects malformed data, rather than silently accepting it, is a meaningful ML-specific CI check, unlike unrelated interface, commit-count or mailing-list checks.

questions.question: A shadow deployment is chosen for testing a new fraud-detection model before it affects any real decisions. Which limitation of shadow deployment must still be accounted for?

options.A: It guarantees the new model is completely safe once the shadow period concludes
options.B: Running it many times and looking at the distribution of outputs
options.C: It always requires significantly more infrastructure than any other testing approach available
options.D: It can only ever be used for models that make no numeric predictions of any kind

questions.explanation: Because shadow mode never actually acts on the new model's outputs, it cannot observe real downstream effects, such as changed user behavior, that only appear once decisions are truly acted upon.

questions.question: Which practice most directly reduces the risk of "training and serving skew," where a model behaves differently in production than expected from testing?

options.A: Testing explicitly with rotated and other transformed variants
options.B: Using two completely independently written and maintained feature computation implementations
options.C: Skipping feature computation entirely during model serving in production
options.D: Increasing the number of features used only during the offline training process

questions.explanation: Skew often arises when training and serving compute the same conceptual feature differently; sharing the actual code or logic between the two pipelines removes that specific source of inconsistency.

questions.question: A team can't define exact expected outputs for an AI classifier during development testing. Which technique best supports meaningful automated checks anyway?

options.A: Asserting only that the program does not crash, with no check of the actual output
options.B: Metamorphic testing, checking relationships between related inputs and their outputs
options.C: Disabling automated testing entirely until an exact oracle becomes available
options.D: Requiring a human to manually approve every single automated test result by hand

questions.explanation: Metamorphic relations provide a practical way to automate meaningful checks even without a precise oracle, which fits development testing far better than manual approval or trivial crash-only checks.

questions.question: Bias is discovered against a subgroup shortly after a model launches. What should be the first response from an ML development testing perspective?

options.A: Unifying the feature logic so both pipelines compute it identically
options.B: Ignore the finding until the next scheduled major model release, whenever that occurs
options.C: Publicly deny that any bias exists until an external party independently proves it
options.D: Immediately delete all records describing the affected subgroup from every dataset

questions.explanation: A responsible first step is to understand how serious and widespread the issue actually is, which then informs a proportionate mitigation, rather than delaying, denying, or taking a drastic unrelated action.

questions.question: Monitoring shows a production model's accuracy decaying gradually, on a roughly weekly basis, since launch. What is the most likely underlying cause?

options.A: A sudden, single, large software defect introduced right at the moment of release
options.B: A one-time hardware failure that occurred on the exact day of the original launch
options.C: An improvement in real-world conditions that is coincidentally being misreported as decay
options.D: Gradual data or concept drift, as real-world patterns slowly diverge from the original training data

questions.explanation: A steady, gradual decline over time is a classic signature of drift, where the world slowly diverges from training-time conditions, distinct from a one-time event like a launch-day defect.

questions.question: Which split strategy suits time-series data, such as sales figures collected daily over several years?

options.A: A chronological split, with all training data occurring strictly before all test data in time
options.B: A purely random split, mixing dates from any point in the whole time series indiscriminately
options.C: A split based only on the alphabetical order of a categorical product-name field
options.D: A split that always uses exactly the most recent single day as the entire training set

questions.explanation: Time-series evaluation needs to respect real-world chronology to avoid the model implicitly learning from the future, so a forward-in-time chronological split is the appropriate strategy, not a random or unrelated split.

questions.question: Model outputs vary from run to run for the same input, due to sampling. What test design accounts for this non-determinism appropriately?

options.A: Disabling all sampling entirely, even in cases where sampling is actually functionally required
options.B: Running the same test multiple times and evaluating the distribution or range of outputs, not just one run
options.C: Fixing the random seed permanently everywhere the model is ever deployed in production
options.D: Running the test exactly once and treating that single result as fully definitive

questions.explanation: Because a single run only samples one possible output, repeated execution and analysis of the resulting distribution gives a much more honest picture of the system's actual behavior than a single sample would.

questions.question: An image classifier mislabels images that have been rotated 90 degrees, though it performs well on upright images. What testing approach would most directly catch this before release?

options.A: Mislabeling risks skipping the oversight the real risk warrants
options.B: Testing only the classifier's inference speed rather than its actual predicted labels
options.C: Testing only whether the classifier's underlying code can be successfully compiled
options.D: Testing only with the exact same set of upright images used originally during training

questions.explanation: A weakness specific to a particular kind of input transformation, like rotation, is only caught by tests that actually include that transformation, which speed or compilation checks would never reveal.

questions.question: Feature distribution shifts between the training and production environments for an ML system. What risk does this create if left unaddressed?

options.A: The shift has no possible effect on the model's behavior in any circumstance whatsoever
options.B: The shift always automatically and immediately improves the model's real-world performance instead
options.C: The model's real-world performance may degrade in ways that offline evaluation on the original data would not reveal
options.D: The shift only ever affects the model's file size, not its actual predictions

questions.explanation: When production data no longer resembles the training distribution, offline metrics computed on the old data become an unreliable guide to actual current performance, which is exactly the risk drift monitoring exists to catch.

questions.question: Training and serving skew is found in a production ML system. Which fix most directly addresses the root cause rather than a symptom?

options.A: Increasing the size of the production serving infrastructure without any other change
options.B: Unifying the feature computation logic so training and serving compute features identically
options.C: Retraining the model more frequently without changing how features are computed at all
options.D: Reducing the number of features used only in the training pipeline, leaving serving unchanged

questions.explanation: Because skew stems from a mismatch in how the same feature is computed in two different pipelines, unifying that computation logic addresses the actual root cause, unlike scaling infrastructure or retraining alone.

questions.question: A hospital deploys a diagnostic AI tool but tells patients it is "just a calculator, not really AI," to avoid triggering stricter internal review procedures reserved for AI systems. What is the concern with this framing from a testing and governance perspective?

options.A: Calling a system a calculator always legally exempts it from any further regulatory scrutiny
options.B: A misheard command causing physical or security harm
options.C: The concern only applies if the tool is later found to contain a functional software defect
options.D: The framing is harmless, since what a system is called never affects how it should be tested

questions.explanation: If a genuinely ML-based system is described as something simpler to dodge stricter review, the testing and oversight it actually needs, given its real technology and risk, might never happen.

questions.question: An AI system for wildfire risk prediction combines a machine-learning model with a hand-coded set of regulatory threshold rules that override the model's output in specific cases. What best describes this system?

options.A: A hybrid AI-based system, combining a learned ML component with conventional rule-based logic
options.B: A system with no AI component at all, since regulatory rules are involved
options.C: A purely narrow AI system, since narrow and hybrid systems are mutually exclusive terms
options.D: A purely rule-based system, since the presence of any override rules removes any AI classification

questions.explanation: Combining a learned model with explicit override rules is a common hybrid design, and it still counts as an AI-based system because its behavior is partly determined by the ML component, even though rules also play a role.

questions.question: A voice assistant's underlying speech-recognition and natural-language-understanding components sit within a broader application that also includes conventional account-management code. Which part of the system is most directly the "AI-based" component?

options.A: Neither part, since a voice assistant can never be classified as any kind of AI system
options.B: The entire application, since any application containing any AI component is entirely rule-based
options.C: The speech-recognition and natural-language-understanding components, whose behavior derives from trained models
options.D: The account-management code, since it manages the most business-critical, sensitive data

questions.explanation: The AI-based classification applies specifically to the components whose behavior is shaped by trained models, here speech recognition and language understanding, while account management remains conventional code.

questions.question: Why might a company choose narrow AI for a specific customer-support task rather than pursuing a more general, broadly capable AI approach?

options.A: Choosing narrow AI removes any need to perform testing of the resulting system at all
options.B: General AI is currently a mature, widely available, off-the-shelf commercial product for any task
options.C: A narrow, task-specific system is typically more practical, reliable and testable for a well-defined task today
options.D: Narrow AI systems are always incapable of achieving any useful level of task performance

questions.explanation: Since general AI remains a research aspiration rather than a deployed reality, task-specific narrow AI is the practical, testable choice for well-defined problems like customer support today.

questions.question: A company's AI ethics board classifies a resume-screening tool as posing significant risk to job applicants' rights and opportunities. Under a risk-tiered regulatory approach, what would this classification most likely require?

options.A: Automatic banning of the tool in every jurisdiction worldwide without any further process
options.B: A requirement that the tool never be updated again once it has passed its first review
options.C: Complete exemption from any testing requirements, since ethics boards replace the need for formal testing
options.D: Enhanced obligations such as risk assessments, documentation and more rigorous testing before and during use

questions.explanation: Higher-risk classifications under risk-tiered frameworks generally trigger stronger obligations, including more thorough risk assessment, documentation and testing, not exemption from oversight.

questions.question: A self-learning fraud-detection system is described by its vendor as requiring "zero maintenance" because it continuously adapts on its own. What testing concern should this specific claim raise?

options.A: Continuous adaptation makes any further testing entirely redundant and unnecessary going forward
options.B: Zero maintenance claims apply only to systems that use absolutely no training data of any kind
options.C: The claim should be fully trusted, since self-learning systems can never develop any new problems once deployed
options.D: A smaller, faster model may trade some accuracy for less resource use

questions.explanation: A system that keeps learning after deployment can drift toward unwanted behavior, such as being manipulated by adversarial inputs it learns from, so "zero maintenance" understates the ongoing monitoring and testing such systems typically need.

questions.question: Which of the following best illustrates the "AI effect" in a software organization's own internal language over time?

options.A: Retraining may be needed to change behavior, not just editing code
options.B: A brand-new generative AI feature is launched and immediately marketed heavily as revolutionary AI technology
options.C: A company raises the price of its AI-labeled product significantly after a successful funding round
options.D: A team decides to rewrite an existing feature using a completely different, unrelated programming language

questions.explanation: The AI effect describes exactly this pattern: a capability once marketed as AI becomes so routine that people stop calling it AI at all, which the aging, no-longer-marketed spam filter exemplifies.

questions.question: A generative AI writing assistant sometimes produces plausible-looking but factually incorrect claims, stated with high apparent confidence. Which quality characteristic is most directly implicated?

options.A: Installability, since factual accuracy has no bearing on how the tool is set up
options.B: Functional correctness (accuracy), since the tool's output does not reliably match ground truth
options.C: Compatibility, since factual accuracy has no relationship to interoperating with other software
options.D: Portability, since correctness has no relationship to installation or migration between environments

questions.explanation: Confidently stated but false output is fundamentally a correctness problem, distinct from characteristics like portability or installability that concern how the system integrates or deploys, not the truth of its output.

questions.question: An organization wants its AI-based loan-approval system to be auditable, meaning a regulator can later reconstruct exactly why a specific decision was made. Which quality characteristic combination is most relevant?

options.A: Time behavior and resource utilization, which concern speed and computational cost, not auditability
options.B: Installability and adaptability, which concern setup and behavior change, not decision justification
options.C: Portability and co-existence, which concern moving or running alongside other unrelated software
options.D: Transparency and explainability, supporting traceable, understandable justification for individual decisions

questions.explanation: Auditability of individual decisions depends on being able to see and explain what drove them, which is exactly what transparency and explainability address, unlike characteristics concerned with deployment, performance or adaptation.

questions.question: A voice-controlled home assistant occasionally responds to a command it misheard by taking a harmful, unintended action, such as unlocking a door. Which quality characteristic most directly relates to preventing this kind of outcome?

options.A: Usability, since the primary concern here is how pleasant the assistant is to interact with
options.B: Portability, since the primary concern here is how easily the assistant moves between devices
options.C: Maintainability, since the primary concern here is how easy the assistant's code is to update
options.D: Safety, since the concern is about preventing physical or security harm from the system's actions

questions.explanation: Preventing harmful physical or security consequences from a misinterpreted command is fundamentally a safety concern, distinct from usability, portability or maintainability, which address different quality aspects.

questions.question: A company claims its facial-recognition system is "unbiased" but has never tested its accuracy separately across different skin tones or lighting conditions. What is the most direct criticism of this claim?

options.A: The claim must be true, since facial-recognition systems are inherently incapable of exhibiting any bias
options.B: Testing across skin tones and lighting conditions is legally forbidden in every jurisdiction
options.C: Without disaggregated testing, there is no actual evidence to support the fairness claim being made
options.D: Fairness can only ever be assessed through a system's marketing materials, not through direct testing

questions.explanation: A fairness claim needs supporting evidence, and without evaluating performance across relevant subgroups and conditions, there is no actual basis for concluding the system is unbiased.

questions.question: A company wants to balance "functional suitability" and "resource efficiency" for an AI feature that must run on low-power mobile devices. What trade-off is most likely to arise?

options.A: Mobile devices always have unlimited computational capacity for running any AI model
options.B: Resource efficiency has no meaningful relationship to a model's size or computational demands
options.C: A smaller, faster, less resource-intensive model may sacrifice some accuracy compared with a larger, more capable one
options.D: Functional suitability and resource efficiency are always perfectly aligned with no possible trade-off

questions.explanation: Constrained device resources often force a choice between a lighter, faster model that fits the device and a larger, more accurate one that may not, which is a classic instance of a genuine quality trade-off.

questions.question: Why might "maintainability" be considered differently for an ML-based component than for conventional, hand-coded software?

options.A: Updating an ML component may require retraining or fine-tuning on new data, not just editing source code
options.B: ML components are always trivially easier to maintain than any conventional software system
options.C: Maintainability is a concept that applies only to systems with absolutely no learning component
options.D: ML components can never be maintained or updated once they have been deployed to production

questions.explanation: Where conventional software is typically changed by editing code directly, an ML component's behavior often needs to change through retraining or fine-tuning on new or corrected data, which is a distinct maintenance path.

questions.question: A company's AI system quality checklist references ISO/IEC 25010 but does not mention ISO/IEC 25059 at all. What gap does this create?

options.A: No gap exists, since ISO/IEC 25010 alone already fully covers every AI-specific quality concern
options.B: ISO/IEC 25059 only applies to systems that have absolutely no software component at all
options.C: Characteristics and considerations specific to AI systems, which ISO/IEC 25059 adds, may not be adequately covered
options.D: Referencing both standards together is explicitly forbidden by international standards bodies

questions.explanation: ISO/IEC 25059 extends the general quality model in ISO/IEC 25010 specifically for AI systems, so relying on the general standard alone risks missing AI-specific characteristics and guidance that the extension provides.

questions.question: A team building a spam classifier decides to try both a simple naive Bayes model and a more complex deep neural network, then compares them on the same held-out test set. What is the primary purpose of this comparison?

options.A: To determine which model was developed first, in strict chronological order
options.B: To determine which model uses a larger number of total lines of source code
options.C: To determine which of the two models was easier and faster to originally implement in code
options.D: Whether given explanations are accurate and genuinely reflect reasoning

questions.explanation: Comparing a simple baseline against a more complex alternative on the same data directly answers whether the complexity is worth it, which is the central purpose of this kind of comparison.

questions.question: A team notices their gradient-boosted model's predictions change substantially depending on the order in which nearly identical training examples were fed into training. What ML concept does this most directly touch on?

options.A: Data drift, which specifically concerns changes in the input distribution after deployment, not training order
options.B: Feature engineering, which specifically concerns how input variables are constructed, not training order
options.C: Label noise, which specifically concerns incorrect labels, not training example ordering
options.D: Model instability or variance, where small differences in training conditions produce meaningfully different models

questions.explanation: Sensitivity to seemingly minor training conditions, like example order, reflects the model's variance or instability, a distinct concept from drift, label noise or feature engineering.

questions.question: An LLM-based coding assistant is given a very low temperature setting for a task requiring the same reliable, predictable code snippet every time. Why is a low temperature appropriate here?

options.A: Lower temperature guarantees the generated code will always be completely free of any defects
options.B: Lower temperature reduces randomness in generation, favoring the most likely, consistent output
options.C: Lower temperature has no effect at all on how consistent or varied the model's output is
options.D: Lower temperature always increases the total number of tokens the model can process

questions.explanation: Since temperature controls sampling randomness, a low value favors the model's most probable, and thus more consistent and predictable, output, which fits a task valuing reliability over creative variation.

questions.question: A model trained to detect manufacturing defects performs very well in the lab but poorly on the factory floor, where lighting and camera angles vary more than in the curated training images. What ML concept best explains this gap?

options.A: The model must have a fundamental bug in its underlying mathematical algorithm
options.B: The factory floor cameras are always technically incompatible with any trained ML model
options.C: The training data was not representative of the real deployment conditions the model actually faces
options.D: Lab and factory performance should always be identical for any correctly trained model

questions.explanation: When training conditions do not match real deployment conditions, a model can perform well in evaluation but poorly in practice, which is a representativeness gap rather than necessarily an algorithmic bug.

questions.question: A team building a churn-prediction model considers using a customer's exact signup date as a raw input feature versus deriving "days since signup" as an engineered feature. Why might the derived feature work better?

options.A: Engineered features always require exactly the same amount of information as raw ones
options.B: Whether this pattern could reflect age-related bias as a signal
options.C: Raw dates are always mathematically impossible for any machine learning model to process
options.D: Feature engineering can only ever be applied to text data, never to date or time values

questions.explanation: A raw date is tied to a specific point in time with little inherent meaning for a new customer, whereas a derived duration like "days since signup" more directly captures a pattern likely related to churn.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why an ensemble of several different models often outperforms any single one of them?

options.A: Ensembles always achieve perfect accuracy by definition, regardless of the individual models used
options.B: The remaining data may no longer represent the true population
options.C: Ensembles are always faster to run at prediction time than any single individual model
options.D: An ensemble is defined as using exactly the same single model duplicated multiple times

questions.explanation: Ensembles work because different models tend to make different kinds of errors, so combining them can smooth out individual weaknesses, which is the typical rationale for why ensembling improves performance.

questions.question: A team must choose between a model that is 2% more accurate but takes 50 times longer to produce a prediction, for a feature requiring real-time response. Which consideration should weigh most heavily in this decision?

options.A: The accuracy figure alone, since higher accuracy should always be chosen regardless of any other factor
options.B: Neither factor matters, since accuracy and latency are always completely unrelated to any real use case
options.C: The latency figure alone, since faster response should always be chosen regardless of any accuracy difference
options.D: Whether users can tolerate the added latency for the given use case, weighed against the modest accuracy gain

questions.explanation: Real-time constraints mean latency directly affects usability, so the decision needs to weigh the actual user tolerance for delay against a modest accuracy improvement, rather than optimizing either metric in isolation.

questions.question: A tester wants to check that a generative image model does not produce a plausible-looking human face for a prompt requesting "an empty room with no people." What testing technique fits this check?

options.A: Cross-validation, which is specific to evaluating a model's generalization across data splits
options.B: A specific negative-scenario check confirming the model correctly avoids generating disallowed content for a given prompt
options.C: A ROC curve analysis, which is specific to evaluating binary classifiers, not generative image tasks
options.D: A confusion matrix analysis, which is specific to evaluating classification, not generative image tasks

questions.explanation: Checking that a generative system correctly refrains from producing specific disallowed content for a given prompt is a targeted negative test, distinct from classification-specific analyses like a confusion matrix or ROC curve.

questions.question: A team testing an AI-based system relies entirely on the development team's own manually-run tests, with no independent review at any stage. What risk does this create, especially for a high-stakes application?

options.A: No risk exists, since developers are always the most qualified people to test their own AI system thoroughly
options.B: Independent review would always duplicate exactly the same tests the developers already ran
options.C: This risk applies only to conventional software and never to any AI-based system
options.D: Shared blind spots and assumptions between the developers and their own tests may let real problems go undetected

questions.explanation: Developers testing only their own work risk sharing the same assumptions that led to any mistakes in the first place, which is exactly the blind spot that independent review is meant to catch, especially for high-stakes systems.

questions.question: Why might a tester specifically log and review cases where an AI-based system's confidence score is very high but the actual output later turns out to be wrong?

options.A: Because reviewing such cases always and immediately fixes the underlying model without any further work
options.B: Because high-confidence wrong answers are impossible and therefore never worth investigating at all
options.C: Because confidence scores have no relationship whatsoever to how much a user should trust an output
options.D: It may learn the timing artifact instead of real fraud signals

questions.explanation: High-confidence errors are particularly risky since users or automated systems relying on confidence to gauge trust could be badly misled, making this exactly the kind of case worth specific investigation.

questions.question: A team testing a medical imaging AI decides to include test cases drawn from underrepresented equipment models and less common patient demographics, beyond the majority represented in typical training data. What does this specifically address?

options.A: The system's raw processing speed under a high volume of simultaneous requests
options.B: The system's basic ability to load and start up correctly, which a smoke test would check instead
options.C: The risk that the system performs worse for cases it saw less of during training and development
options.D: The system's compatibility with a specific brand of database management software

questions.explanation: Deliberately testing underrepresented equipment and demographics targets exactly the risk that a system trained mostly on majority cases performs worse for the cases it saw less of, a common and important AI-specific risk.

questions.question: Why might testers use "differential testing" between an older and newer version of an AI-based system, examining every input where the two disagree?

options.A: To systematically surface behavioral changes, intended or not, introduced by the newer version
options.B: To measure only the newer version's raw processing speed, and nothing about its correctness
options.C: To avoid the need to define any expected result for any of the disagreeing inputs
options.D: To guarantee that the newer version always agrees with the older version on every single input

questions.explanation: Comparing where two versions disagree directly surfaces behavioral changes, which the team can then judge as intentional improvements or unintended regressions, without needing a full independent oracle for every case.

questions.question: A tester wants to verify that a content-moderation AI system correctly identifies borderline cases that are neither clearly acceptable nor clearly prohibited. What test design approach best targets this?

options.A: Testing only content that has already been reviewed and approved by a human moderator beforehand
options.B: Deliberately including ambiguous, borderline examples in the test set rather than only clear-cut cases
options.C: Skipping ambiguous cases entirely, since they can never have a meaningful expected classification
options.D: Testing only with the clearest, most obvious examples of both acceptable and prohibited content

questions.explanation: Since borderline cases are exactly where a moderation system is most likely to struggle, deliberately including them in the test design directly targets that risk, unlike testing only unambiguous examples.

questions.question: A team testing a self-driving perception model wants to verify not just accuracy, but how the system behaves when its camera input is briefly and completely obscured, such as by sudden dense fog. What kind of testing does this represent?

options.A: Compatibility testing focused on integration with unrelated third-party software
options.B: Standard functional testing under normal, unobstructed operating conditions only
options.C: Robustness testing under a specific, realistic degraded-input scenario
options.D: Usability testing focused on how a human passenger perceives the vehicle's interior

questions.explanation: Testing behavior under a realistic but degraded sensor condition, like sudden obstruction, is a robustness concern, distinct from ordinary functional testing under clean, expected conditions.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: A team collecting training images for a wildlife-identification model realizes almost all images were taken during daytime in clear weather. What input-data testing concern does this raise?

options.A: No concern at all, since lighting and weather conditions never affect an image classification model's behavior
options.B: A representativeness gap, since the model may perform poorly under nighttime or adverse-weather conditions it rarely saw
options.C: A data-poisoning concern, since daytime images are inherently more likely to have been deliberately corrupted
options.D: A labeling concern, since daytime images are inherently more likely to contain incorrect species labels

questions.explanation: A dataset skewed toward one set of conditions, like clear daytime weather, risks leaving the model poorly prepared for the different conditions, such as night or storms, it will actually face in the field.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: A tester reviewing a customer dataset finds that "state" values include both full names like "California" and abbreviations like "CA" for the same actual state. What data-quality issue does this represent?

options.A: Inconsistent formatting or representation of the same underlying value across records
options.B: Label noise, since state fields are never used as labels for a classification task
options.C: Data drift, which specifically concerns changes in data that occur only after model deployment
options.D: Missing values, since every one of the affected records technically has a non-empty state field

questions.explanation: Different representations of the same real value, like full names versus abbreviations, is a formatting inconsistency, which can cause a model to treat semantically identical values as distinct categories.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: A dataset intended to train a resume-screening model contains gaps in employment history that, upon investigation, correlate strongly with a candidate's age. What should this correlation prompt testers to investigate?

options.A: Whether employment history should be removed as a feature only for candidates over fifty
options.B: Whether the dataset should immediately be doubled in size without any further changes
