options.C: Whether this pattern could introduce or reflect age-related bias if used as a predictive signal
options.D: Whether the gaps should be filled in using entirely random, unrelated numeric values

questions.explanation: A feature or pattern correlated with a protected or sensitive characteristic like age is a classic pathway for a model to learn a proxy for that characteristic, warranting fairness-focused investigation.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: A team preparing a dataset for a customer-sentiment model discovers that reviews mentioning a competitor's product name are far more likely to have been manually removed before labeling than reviews that do not mention it. What risk does this selective removal create?

options.A: The removal only matters if it affects more than half of the total dataset's records
options.B: No risk exists, since removing any records from a dataset always improves the trained model's accuracy
options.C: The remaining dataset may no longer represent the true population of reviews, biasing what the model learns
options.D: Selective removal always and only affects the model's training speed, never its actual behavior

questions.explanation: Removing records based on a hidden, non-random criterion, like mentioning a competitor, changes what the remaining data represents, which can bias what the model learns without anyone intending it to.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: Why might input data testing specifically check the encoding of categorical variables, such as verifying that "Yes"/"No" values are not accidentally mixed with "1"/"0" values for the same underlying field?

options.A: A value like 70 could mean two different things without labeling
options.B: Categorical encoding has no bearing whatsoever on how a machine learning model processes a feature
options.C: Encoding checks are only relevant to numeric fields, never to categorical ones
options.D: Mixed encodings always automatically and correctly resolve themselves during model training

questions.explanation: If "Yes" and "1" are not recognized as equivalent, a model may treat them as entirely separate categories, fragmenting a pattern that should have been learned as one consistent signal.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: A team building a fraud model finds that fraudulent transactions in their dataset are, coincidentally, almost all recorded a few seconds faster than legitimate ones due to how the logging system happened to work, unrelated to actual fraud behavior. What risk does this create?

options.A: This risk can only ever occur in models used outside of the financial services industry
options.B: The timing pattern will always improve the model's ability to generalize to future, unseen fraud
options.C: No risk exists, since a model can never learn from any pattern that is not the intended, genuine signal
options.D: The model may learn to key off this incidental timing artifact rather than genuine indicators of fraud

questions.explanation: A model trained on this data risks learning a spurious shortcut, the logging artifact, instead of real fraud indicators, which would fail to generalize once that artifact is absent or changes.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: Why should testers verify that a dataset's units of measurement are consistent, such as confirming all weight values are recorded in kilograms rather than a mix of kilograms and pounds?

options.A: Mixed units always cause a training pipeline to immediately crash with an unambiguous, easily caught error
options.B: Verifying units is unnecessary as long as the dataset's overall record count is sufficiently large
options.C: Unit consistency only ever matters for datasets used in scientific research, not for any commercial product
options.D: Mixed units without clear labeling can cause numerically similar-looking values to actually mean very different things

questions.explanation: A value like "70" meaning kilograms in some rows and pounds in others would silently distort what the model learns unless the inconsistency is caught, since it may not cause an obvious crash.
